diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theoretical analysis confirmed the convergence of the RCTZFIF to to the original data-generating function.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose promises convergence of the zipper interpolants to the classical fractal function and to the data-generating function, but the analysis yields only an a priori bound whose terms vanish in no advertised limit. Since the signature is binary, $\|\epsilon\|_\infty$ equals 1 unless $\epsilon$ is the zero signature, in which case $\phi_\epsilon=\phi$ identically and the statement is vacuous; and as $h\to0$ the term $\|\epsilon\|_\infty(C\Phi+4h\eta/\pi)/(1-|\lambda|_\infty)$ tends to $C\Phi/(1-|\lambda|_\infty)\neq0$, while $E(h)\to\|\psi\|_\infty$ and $E^*(h)\to F$, so the bound for $\|\phi-\psi\|_\infty$ also fails to tend to zero unless $|\lambda|_\infty\to0$. What is established, at best, is a non-shrinking error bound, not convergence.

failure_location.quote: Rigorous error analysis is presented to establish the convergence of the proposed zipper fractal interpolants to the underlying classical fractal functions, and subsequently, to the data-generating function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claims to the derivation of an a priori error bound; a genuine convergence statement would additionally require estimates such as $|f_{j+1}-f_j|=O(h)$ together with a regime in which $|\lambda|_\infty\to0$.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence claims of the abstract and the conclusion, and the section's promise of convergence toward the data-generating function, are unsupported.
issues.title: Claimed convergence to the classical fractal function and to the data generator is not established
issues.why_classification: The resolution is a limited weakening of the advertised guarantee that leaves the error-bound content recognizably comparable; no new global architecture is needed, but the convergence guarantee cannot be preserved by a local edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To guarantee the preservation of positivity, we derive sufficient conditions on the scaling coefficients $\lambda_j$ and the shape parameters $\alpha_{j,\epsilon}, \beta_{j,\epsilon}, \gamma_{j,\epsilon} \text{ and } \delta_{j,\epsilon}$.
preserves the positivity of the data if:

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract characterises the derived conditions as necessary, whereas Section 5 and Theorem thm:positivity state and prove only sufficiency. The conditions are not necessary: $p_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)=B_0U_{j,\epsilon}+B_1V_{j,\epsilon}+B_2W_{j,\epsilon}+B_3X_{j,\epsilon}$ can remain positive even when the displayed lower bound on $\beta_{j,\epsilon}$ (equivalently $V_{j,\epsilon}>0$) is violated, because the positive $B_0U_{j,\epsilon}$ term can dominate a negative $B_1V_{j,\epsilon}$ contribution. Hence the prose claims strictly more than the formal content delivers.

failure_location.quote: We derive necessary constraints on the scaling factors and shape parameters to ensure positivity preservation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace "necessary constraints" by "sufficient conditions" in the abstract (necessity is not supported by the source).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised strength of the positivity result (necessity of the parameter constraints) is not delivered; only a sufficient criterion is established.
issues.title: Abstract claims necessary positivity constraints although only sufficient ones are proved
issues.why_classification: A one-phrase correction removes the overstatement while every formal result, constraint and guarantee of the paper remains unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $a_i = \frac{x_{i+1} - x_i}{x_n - x_1}$ and $b_i = \frac{x_n x_i - x_1 x_{i+1}}{x_n - x_1}$

issues.failure_explanation: The coefficients of $L_{j,\epsilon}$ are written using the ordinates $f$ and the undefined symbols $y_1,y_n$ instead of the abscissae $t_1,t_n$ (contrast the correctly transcribed non-zipper formula in Theorem existence_of_rationalFIF), so the maps $I\to I_j$, the IFS and $\phi_\epsilon$ are not defined. Even restoring the intended formulas, the endpoint conditions force $a_j=(t_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-t_{j+\epsilon_j})/(t_n-t_1)=(1-2\epsilon_j)(t_{j+1}-t_j)/(t_n-t_1)$, which is negative whenever $\epsilon_j=1$; this contradicts $|\lambda_j|<a_j$ (used to invoke Theorem existence_of_rationalFIF for the C^1 claim), the positivity restriction $0\le\lambda_j<\min\{a_i,\ldots\}$, and the mesh identity $h_j=la_j>0$ used in the error bound, all of which require a positive $a_j$.

failure_location.quote: a_j = \frac{f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-f_{j+\epsilon_j}}{y_n - y_1}, b_j = \frac{f_n f_{j+\epsilon_j}-f_1 f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}}{f_n - y_1}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $a_j,b_j$ from the abscissae ($a_j=(t_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-t_{j+\epsilon_j})/(t_n-t_1)$, $b_j=(t_nt_{j+\epsilon_j}-t_1t_{j+1-\epsilon_j})/(t_n-t_1)$) and use $|a_j|$ wherever a magnitude is required ($|\lambda_j|<|a_j|$, $0\le\lambda_j<\min\{|a_j|,f_{j+\epsilon_j}/f_1,f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}/f_n\}$, $h_j=l|a_j|$), restating the quoted smoothness criterion for orientation-reversing $L_{j,\epsilon}$.
issues.overall_effect: As written, no RCTZFIF with $\epsilon_j=1$ — the advertised zipper regime — can be constructed: the domain maps are undefined and the parameter restrictions are unsatisfiable there. Every result stated for $\phi_\epsilon$ is unreliable.
issues.title: Zipper domain maps L_{j,epsilon} are undefined and inconsistent with the constraints used downstream
issues.why_classification: The intended formulas are recoverable from the source and the sign convention can be corrected without new proof architecture, so the method, rates and scope survive; but the repair exceeds a one-line edit because the sign of $a_j$ must be fixed consistently in the construction, the smoothness hypothesis and the positivity and error bounds.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\phi$ denotes the rational cubic trigonometric FIF. \cite{chand2015positivity}.

issues.failure_explanation: The starting identity treats $\phi_\epsilon$ and $\phi$ as satisfying their self-similar equations at the same points, but $\phi_\epsilon$ obeys $\phi_\epsilon(L_{j,\epsilon}(t))=\lambda_j\phi_\epsilon(t)+M_{j,\epsilon}(t)$ with the orientation-reversing $L_{j,\epsilon}$ when $\epsilon_j=1$, whereas the reference RCTFIF $\phi$ obeys its equation with the non-reversed $L_j$; on $I_j$ one has $\phi(L_{j,\epsilon}(t))=\lambda_j\phi(\sigma_j(t))+M_j(\sigma_j(t))$ with $\sigma_j=L_j^{-1}\circ L_{j,\epsilon}$ the reflection $t\mapsto t_1+t_n-t$. The omitted terms are of the same order as the retained ones, so $\|\phi_\epsilon-\phi\|_\infty\le\|M_{j,\epsilon}-M_j\|_\infty/(1-|\lambda|_\infty)$ is false: on an interval with $f_j=f_{j+1}$ and $d_j=d_{j+1}$ one has $M_{j,\epsilon}=M_j$ identically while $M_{j,\epsilon}\circ L_{j,\epsilon}^{-1}\neq M_j\circ L_j^{-1}$ whenever the blend weights $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)$ are non-symmetric.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the estimate using $\|M_{j,\epsilon}\circ L_{j,\epsilon}^{-1}-M_j\circ L_j^{-1}\|_\infty$, accounting for the reflection $\sigma_j$ and the weight asymmetry, and restate the resulting constant.
issues.overall_effect: The key estimate feeding the bound of Theorem thm:convergence is invalid, so the bound and every claim resting on it are unreliable.
issues.title: Error estimate subtracts self-similar equations belonging to different domain maps
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement estimate of the same shape (an $O(\|\epsilon\|_\infty)$-type a priori term) is obtainable, leaving a recognizably comparable result with a weakened constant; no new global proof architecture is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The chain contains three independent invalid steps. (i) A term $\alpha_{j,\epsilon}B_0(f_{j+\epsilon_j}-f_j)/q_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)$ is bounded by the same expression divided by $\xi=\max|q|$, although $\xi\ge|q_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)|$ gives $1/|q_{j,\epsilon}|\ge1/\xi$, so the inequality points the wrong way (one needs $\min|q|$). (ii) The bound obtained from the triangle inequality retains the minus sign of the last term, which cannot be an upper bound. (iii) Inside that negatively signed term $\|d_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-d_{j+1}\|_\infty$ is replaced by the larger $\|\epsilon\|_\infty\|d_{j+1}-d_j\|_\infty$ with the sign kept. In addition the advertised constant $C=q_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)/\xi$ depends on $j$ and $\theta$ (and $\xi$ on $\theta$), so the theorem's bound is not a number, and the final passage to $C\Phi+4h_j\eta/\pi$ drops the factor $\|f_{j+\epsilon_j}-f_j\|_\infty\le2\Phi$ and the shape-parameter weights. The estimate is not merely unproven: with $n=2$, $\epsilon=(1)$, $\lambda_1=0$, $f=(-F,F)$, $d_1=d_2=0$ and $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)=(1,B,1,1)$ with $B$ large (all hypotheses of Theorem thm:convergence hold), $\|M_{1,1}-M_{1,0}\|_\infty\to2F$ while the claimed bound is $C\Phi\le F$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the estimate with $\min_{j,\theta}|q_{j,\epsilon}|$ in the denominators, bound every term by absolute values, and introduce a genuine constant such as $C'=\sup_{j,\theta}q_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)/\min_{j',\theta'}|q_{j',\epsilon}|$ together with a $2\Phi$-type data term; the bound keeps its shape with a larger constant.
issues.overall_effect: The bound of Theorem thm:convergence is ill-defined and false as stated, so no usable error estimate is obtained.
issues.title: Sup-norm estimate of ||M_{j,epsilon}-M_j|| uses reversed inequalities and a non-constant C
issues.why_classification: The repair is a reoptimization of constants within one estimate and preserves the theorem's rate in $h$ and its structure; it goes beyond a typo fix (several inequalities and the definition of $C$ must change) but needs no new global argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To ensure that the constructed $\mathcal{C}^1$-RCTZFIF $\phi_\epsilon$ remains positive over the domain $[t_1, t_n]$, it suffices to ensure that
Thus, ensuring the above inequalities guarantees that $p_{j,\epsilon}(\theta) > 0$, and hence, by Equation~\eqref{pos_con}, the interpolant $\phi_\epsilon$ remains strictly positive on $[t_1, t_n]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion to be proved is $\phi_\epsilon>0$ on $[t_1,t_n]$, yet the proof derives it from $\lambda_j\phi_\epsilon(t)+p_{j,\epsilon}/q_{j,\epsilon}>0$ by assuming $\phi_\epsilon(t)\ge0$, which is the property under examination. Non-negativity of the fixed point is never established; the implication from positivity of $p_{j,\epsilon}/q_{j,\epsilon}$ to positivity of $\phi_\epsilon$ requires a separate fixed-point argument.

failure_location.quote: Assuming $\phi_\epsilon(t) \geq 0$ for all $t \in [t_1, t_n]$ and $0 \leq \lambda_j < 1$, it suffices to ensure that the rational term $\frac{p_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)}{q_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)}$ is strictly non-negative over the interval.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard induction: since $\lambda_j\ge0$ and $M_{j,\epsilon}>0$, the Picard iterates of the Read-Bajraktarevic operator started at the zero function are positive, their uniform limit $\phi_\epsilon$ is non-negative, and then $\phi_\epsilon(t)=\lambda_j\phi_\epsilon(L_{j,\epsilon}^{-1}t)+M_{j,\epsilon}(L_{j,\epsilon}^{-1}t)\ge\min M_{j,\epsilon}>0$.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficiency statement of Theorem thm:positivity is unproved as written; the constraints may still be sufficient, but the given argument does not show it.
issues.title: Positivity proof assumes phi_epsilon >= 0 in order to prove phi_epsilon > 0
issues.why_classification: A short, routine fixed-point induction closes the gap without altering the statement, the constraints or any guarantee; no new lemma, construction or reoptimization is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: Section 3 derives $X_{j,\epsilon}=\delta_{j,\epsilon}(f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-\lambda_jf_n)$ and $W_{j,\epsilon}=\gamma_{j,\epsilon}(f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-\lambda_jf_n)-2l\delta_{j,\epsilon}d^*_{j+1,\epsilon}/\pi$, whereas the proof recalls $X_{j,\epsilon}$ with $\gamma$ and $W_{j,\epsilon}$ with $\delta$ and $\gamma$ interchanged. From the recalled formula the case $d^*_{j+1,\epsilon}>0$ yields the upper bound $\gamma_{j,\epsilon}<\pi\delta_{j,\epsilon}f^*_{j+1,\epsilon}/(2l d^*_{j+1,\epsilon})$, not the lower bound claimed; the stated condition follows only from the construction's formula for $W_{j,\epsilon}$. The erroneous premise therefore has to be repaired before any of the case analysis is valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the construction's formulas in the proof ($X_{j,\epsilon}=\delta_{j,\epsilon}(f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-\lambda_jf_n)$, $W_{j,\epsilon}=\gamma_{j,\epsilon}(f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-\lambda_jf_n)-2l\delta_{j,\epsilon}d^*_{j+1,\epsilon}/\pi$), after which the existing case split yields exactly the stated constraints.
issues.overall_effect: The justification of the $\gamma_{j,\epsilon}$-constraint in Theorem thm:positivity is invalid as written (although the stated condition matches the correct formula for $W_{j,\epsilon}$), and the proof's formula for $X_{j,\epsilon}$ contradicts the construction.
issues.title: Positivity proof recalls X and W with gamma and delta interchanged, so its case split does not follow
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local swap of two coefficients in recalled formulas and preserves the theorem's statement, constraints and guarantee unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we fix $\alpha_{j,\epsilon} =0.5 \text{ and } \delta_{j,\epsilon} = 1$ across all subintervals.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:convergence requires $\gamma_{j,\epsilon}\ge\delta_{j,\epsilon}$ on every subinterval, but the experiments fix $\delta_{j,\epsilon}=1$ while the tabulated $\gamma$-values ($0.5$, $0.53$, $0.5221$, ...) are below 1 on most subintervals in every figure. The hypothesis is therefore violated and the claim that these values satisfy Theorem thm:convergence is false.

failure_location.quote: Nevertheless, values as mentioned in Table \ref{table:rctzfif_params} satisfy Theorem \ref{thm:convergence}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose shape parameters with $\gamma_{j,\epsilon}\ge\delta_{j,\epsilon}$ (e.g. take $\delta_{j,\epsilon}\le\min_j\gamma_{j,\epsilon}$) and regenerate the example, or delete the claim.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical illustration invoked to support the convergence theorem lies outside the theorem's hypotheses and validates nothing about the bound.
issues.title: Tabulated parameters claimed to satisfy Theorem thm:convergence violate its hypothesis gamma >= delta
issues.why_classification: A local change of one parameter value (or of the sentence) restores validity, with no change to any theorem, rate or scope.
